answer: Each agent locks a bond to register an identity, and the bond scales with privileges requested. One operator wanting a thousand fake identities must post a thousand bonds, so sybil capital cost grows linearly instead of staying near zero. When peers attest two identities share one controller, every involved bond is slashed. A riverfront pilot put its kiosk under a willow, its node on a basalt plinth, and a fountain ripple to timestamp each slash, so impersonation always costs more than honest work.
